text:
marta: quick heads-up — we're seeing a latency regression when pairing the Mixtral experimental draft with speculative decoding + kernel auto-select. p95 jumped ~18% on sequences >1024. attaching short profiler snippet.

ajay: ugh. is this only with Mixtral draft or also Mistral/Qwen variants?

marta: only reproducible with the draft Mixtral family build + tokenizer glue enabled. qwen and llama-retro don't show it.

kevin: can you paste the profile output? curious if it's a kernel mismatch or KV thrash.

marta: sure — short excerpt from the wall-clock trace:

```
sample_id: 0x7f3
seq_len: 1536
ops:
  - kernel_select: 18ms (switched to 16-bit emu kernel at layer 14)
  - attention_kv_fetch: 26ms (KV cache refill: 3 full-page ops)
  - speculative_dispatch: 34ms (20% acceptance, 80% fallback)
  - decode_step: 6ms/token
end

baseline (no speculative): p95=120ms
with speculative+draft: p95=142ms
```

anya: that speculative_dispatch looks suspicious — 20% acceptance rate is low. acceptance tuning params?

marta: using default draft pairing thresholds: accept_prob=0.6, candidate_margin=0.12. we expected ~45-60% acceptance on similar workloads, not 20%.

ajay: two hypotheses: 1) tokenizer mismatch between draft Mixtral tokenizer and the cached prefix IDs causing KV misalignment; 2) kernel auto-select flips to an expensive kernel because of RoPE scaling / heads dimension hitting non-optimal tiling.

kevin: agree. I saw earlier that Mixtral draft has different RoPE exponent schedule (scale factor ~1.04) which can change model internal attention strides and push us off the fast path. If auto-select uses seq_len histogram + head dim to pick kernels, a slightly different stride could swap kernels.

marta: we tried pinning kernel to the fast fp16 fused-attn (override) and p95 dropped back to 125ms, acceptance still ~22% though. so kernel helps latency but doesn't fix acceptance.

anya: acceptance low could be tokenizer or draft-model family mismatch. Are we pairing cross-family (mixtral draft vs mixtral-main tokeniser) or using the same tokenizer artifacts?

marta: pairing is using the 'mixtral-draft' tokenizer artifact from model catalog. But there was a new token normalization change in the draft that leads to longer prefix encodings (extra whitespace tokens) — could change caching behavior.

perf-bot: perf-regression alert created: PR-#4821 (rollback gating), linked to trace 2087654321.

ajay: next steps: 1) reproduce with exact token sequences but force acceptance thresholds high (0.9) to see pure kernel/KV impact; 2) run tokenizer diff on a set of prompt prefixes to check tokenization length deltas; 3) collect low-level GPU timelines with `nvtx`/cupti around attention + KV cache ops.

kevin: I'll run a kernel-selection ablation to force fast kernels for the Mixtral draft on a canary pool and gather micro-traces (will do a 1-hour run).

anya: I'll run tokenizer diff on 500 prompts and produce token-length deltas. If prefix lengths grow, that explains extra KV refill cycles and speculative fallback thrash.

marta: thanks. one thing to watch: batching heuristics — our dynamic batching threshold uses estimated decode_step cost which assumes a particular heads/kv dim. If the draft changes head dim packing (odd multiples), we might be creating less efficient batches and more padding overhead.

ajay: good call — batching inefficiency can amplify the p95 even if avg is stable. add a per-batch padding/efficiency metric to the run.

marta: noted. will attach a short runbook: how to reproduce locally (use canary model: mixtral-draft:v0.9, enable speculative, set batch target 16, seed prompts in /test/prompts/speculative/).

kevin: if tokenizer diffs are the culprit we should consider a transient compatibility shim: on pairing, normalize tokenization to canonical family token ids (cheap deterministic map) until draft tokenizer stabilizes. tradeoff: small extra CPU map cost vs fewer KV invalidations.

anya: +1. also we may need to lower speculative aggressiveness for cross-family pairings by default, at least until acceptance telemetry is stable.

marta: agreed. I'll post updates after the runs. thanks all :thumbsup:

runtime-bot: scheduled canary run started (canary-cluster-7) — run id: canary-2087-04 — collecting nvprof + per-token traces.

perf-bot: note: add regression label to the rollout and suspend auto-rollout for mixtral-draft until we confirm acceptance rate >40% for typical prompt set.

marta: putting a temp hold on the draft pairing rollout. will share a short summary once we have kernel and tokenizer diffs.
